key_insight: Linking real field flips to their preceding access history would ground hammer and refresh margins in measured, workload-specific distributions instead of worst-case assumptions.
killer_doubt: DDR5 on-die ECC hides single-bit flips from host triggers; field errors (Google 2009: ~8% of DIMMs/year) are dominated by hard faults, so hammer/retention events stay sparse.
decisive_experiment: Before building interposers, mine 6 months of MCE/ECS logs plus PEBS access samples on ~200 partner servers; build the DDR5 interposer only if >100 non-hard-fault events appear. ~$100k.
prior_art: Field studies (Google 2009, Facebook 2015, AMD/LANL 2015); ETH DRAM Bender/SoftMC lab characterization; DDR protocol-analyzer interposers (FuturePlus, Nexus).

key_insight: In HBM, one bad die or channel after CoWoS bonding scraps a whole GPU package; host-visible channel/bank disable rescues far more value there than DDR die binning.
killer_doubt: Mature DRAM yields leave only a few % of dies failing after redundancy, not the claimed 10-20%; PPR and OS page offlining already map out small fails.
decisive_experiment: Buy ~1,000 reject DDR5 components and scrapped HBM stacks; map failure locality on an FPGA tester to measure the share confined to <=2 mats or one pseudo-channel. ~$150k.
prior_art: DDR4/5 post-package repair; Linux page offlining (Facebook 2015); partial-good down-bins; H100 ships 5 of 6 HBM sites; X-PPR (via search snippet).

key_insight: Real sense amps, ECC and refresh logic under real BEOL oxide arrays for tens of $k: the shared test vehicle the top triage cells (N-04, N-43, N-62) need.
killer_doubt: Pad-level coupling adds ~0.1-1 pF per line versus a 35 fF bitline; charge-sense realism needs <=5 um top-metal access on diced die, hard for university CMP.
decisive_experiment: One open-PDK shuttle with SA/ECC tiles exposing a 5 um-pitch top-metal grid; post-process a 1 kb IGZO 1T1C or 2T0C array at <=350 C; measure sense margin and retention tail. ~$80k.
prior_art: Stanford/MIT/SkyWater monolithic 3D (DARPA 3DSoC); BEOL IGZO-on-CMOS at imec, Georgia Tech, Purdue; SkyWater S130 ReRAM option.

key_insight: Parametron-style bistability makes every cell self-restoring with no row-by-row refresh, which in principle frees leakage specs and removes refresh periphery.
killer_doubt: Common plate is ~17 uF per 16 Gb die; a 1 V, 100 kHz pump burns ~1.7 W versus ~12 mW for refresh today, before crosspoint sneak paths.
decisive_experiment: SPICE plus a 4x4 discrete varactor-diode array on a PCB: show two stable fixed points under plate AC drive and measure pump power per cell and noise margin versus frequency. ~$30k.
prior_art: Goto's parametron (1954); TI tunneling-based SRAM with RTD bistability and leakage-balanced standby (van der Wagt, 1999).

key_insight: Reliability data and qualified second sources, not only physics, gate alternative memories; an open qualification line attacks that shared bottleneck.
killer_doubt: Premise weak: Z-RAM and T-RAM faded after AMD, Hynix and GlobalFoundries trials, largely on scaled-node retention/variability; their 1998-2010 filings expire by ~2030 anyway.
decisive_experiment: A $50k audit: for each dead refresh-free venture, document failure cause and patent expiry; proceed only if >=3 died of data/qualification gaps on still-live patents.
prior_art: SRC/NSTC programs and JEDEC qualification norms; Z-RAM licensed by AMD and Hynix, then dropped; T-RAM with GlobalFoundries; standard patent pools.

key_insight: Regenerable AI data (KV/prefix caches) turns memory errors into cache misses: CRC-only blocks on non-ECC, recycled or relaxed-refresh DIMMs, with recompute as the repair path.
killer_doubt: Active KV rows are re-read every ~20-50 ms decode step, already self-refreshing; gains confine to idle prefix-cache tiers and ~12-25% ECC-chip savings.
decisive_experiment: Run vLLM+LMCache with a TB-scale CPU-DRAM prefix tier on non-ECC/recycled DIMMs at 4-8x tREFI plus fault injection; measure CRC hits, recompute overhead, output quality and $/GB versus ECC RDIMM. ~$150k.
prior_art: Kelle (2025) pairs relaxed eDRAM refresh with KV recomputation (via search snippet); EDEN (2019), Flikker (2011); parity-refetch L1 caches.

key_insight: NAND-style read-retry and drift tables in updatable firmware could let oxide BEOL cells with hydrogen/PBTI Vt drift ship before full characterization.
killer_doubt: Works only if drift is deterministic and learnable; random telegraph or VRT-like jumps beyond the ~20 mV multi-level budget defeat fleet-learned models.
decisive_experiment: Stress 64 kb IGZO gain-cell arrays at 85-110 C for 1,000 h; fit a drift model on half the dies and test whether firmware reference tracking holds raw BER <1e-4 on the rest. ~$250k.
prior_art: NAND read-retry tables and FTL firmware updates (all SSD vendors); Astera Labs COSMOS fleet telemetry for CXL; DDR5 ECS error counters.

key_insight: Rank refresh is set by its worst die; matching dies by retention class lets most ranks run 2-4x longer tREFI with assembly-flow changes only.
killer_doubt: Variable retention time: cells jump retention states by >10x over time (Liu, ISCA 2013), so static die binning at 256 ms is unsafe without online profiling or ECC.
decisive_experiment: Bin 200 DDR5 dies by retention at 85 C, then re-test monthly for 6 months on an FPGA tester; count class downgrades caused by VRT. ~$120k.
prior_art: RAIDR (2012), AVATAR (2015), REAPER (2017) retention-aware refresh with profiling/ECC; Liu ISCA 2013 VRT study; vendor power/speed binning.

key_insight: Speculative decoding's verifier rejects any token a memory error corrupts, so draft models can run on weak or relaxed-refresh DRAM at zero correctness cost.
killer_doubt: Draft models and their caches are ~1-5% of inference memory and must sit beside the target model in HBM for latency; the weak-bin outlet is tiny.
decisive_experiment: Inject DRAM-like bit errors into a 1B draft model's weights and KV at BER 1e-9 to 1e-5 in vLLM; measure acceptance-rate loss and throughput. ~$10k.
prior_art: Speculative decoding (Leviathan 2023, Chen 2023); EDEN approximate DRAM for DNNs (2019). The combination: none found.

key_insight: NAND playbook for DRAM: a mature-node CXL controller with strong ECC makes rejects and relaxed refresh usable, and gives new oxide/3D cells a raw-BER-1e-4 landing zone (N-62).
killer_doubt: 4 KB codewords make each random 64 B write a 4 KB read-modify-write (64x traffic) unless the SRAM buffer coalesces; VRT may push raw BER past 1e-4 at 8x tREFI.
decisive_experiment: FPGA CXL card with BCH/LDPC over commodity and reject DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs at 4-8x tREFI, 85 C: log raw-BER tail incl. VRT for weeks, post-ECC errors past 1e15 bits, bandwidth on real traces. ~$400k.
prior_art: Hi-ECC (2010), ArchShield (2013), LOT-ECC (2012); X-PPR recycled-DDR4 CXL repair (2025, via search snippet); Microchip/Astera CXL controllers. LDPC plus relaxed refresh: none found.

key_insight: Decorrelating vendor-systematic failure modes across a codeword's chips is the right instinct for qualifying new second-source and U.S. dies.
killer_doubt: All chips in a rank get identical commands; a vendor-specific TRR bypass hits that vendor's 3-5 chips of a 10-chip codeword at once, beyond chipkill's 1-chip correction.
decisive_experiment: Build mixed-vendor DDR5 RDIMMs; run TRRespass/U-TRR patterns on an FPGA tester and count codewords with >1 failing chip versus single-vendor modules. ~$150k.
prior_art: Chipkill (IBM, 1997); vendor-specific TRR bypass patterns (TRRespass 2020, U-TRR 2021); field studies showing vendor-correlated faults.

key_insight: Transistorless 3D magnetic bits from one hole etch, with unlimited endurance and no refresh, would clear the triage's write-endurance wall via magnetic order.
killer_doubt: A 5 nm film round a 40 nm pillar links ~2e-16 Wb per bit, ~0.4 uV inductive signal; coincident writes need ~1 mA per pillar, ~8e7 A/cm2.
decisive_experiment: Fabricate 10-tier test pillars (ALD NiFe/CoFeB liner in 40-100 nm holes) at a university fab; measure write current, half-select disturb and per-bit AMR/inductive read SNR. ~$300k.
prior_art: Plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, 1960s); IBM racetrack (Parkin); this project's N-82 racetrack-in-capacitor-hole; 3D domain-wall shift registers.
